subject: general
question:
Match the points under List I with those under List II. 

 
 

 
 
**List-I (Instrument)**

 
 
 
**List-II (Use)**

 
 
 

 
 
(1)

 
 Sextant
 
 
a.

 
 Measures the angle between two visible objects
 
 

 
 
(2)

 
 Udometer
 
 
b.

 
 Measures small quantities of radiant heat
 
 

 
 
(3)

 
 Thermopile
 
 
c.

 
 Measures the temperature of a surface
 
 

 
 
(4)

 
 Pyrometer
 
 
d.

 
 Measures the amount of rainfall
solution:
The correct answer is __**1 - a, 2 - d, 3 - b, 4 - c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Sextant Measures the angle between two visible objects:**

 
 
• The sextant is a **navigational instrument used primarily to measure the angle between two visible objects.**
 
• The primary use of a sextant is in navigation, to measure the angle between an astronomical object and the horizon for the purposes of celestial navigation.
 
• The name **"sextant" originates from the Latin word "sextus", meaning "one-sixth".**
 
• This is because the instrument's arc **spans 60 degrees or one-sixth of a full circle.**
 
• The sextant **allows navigators to determine their latitude while at sea or in flight by accurately measuring the angles between the sun and the horizon or between stars and the horizon.**
 
 
 
• **Udometer Measures the amount of rainfall:**
 
 
• An udometer,** more commonly known as a rain gauge, is a type of instrument used by meteorologists and hydrologists to gather and measure the amount of liquid precipitation (rainfall)** over a set period of time.
 
• It's a crucial tool for **weather prediction, scientific research, and for farmers and gardeners to determine if they need to water their crops or gardens.**
 
• This device simply measures the** precipitation in millimetres in height collected on each square meter during a certain period, equivalent to litres per square meter.**
 
 
 
• **Thermopile Measures small quantities of radiant heat:**
 
 
• A thermopile is an electronic device that converts thermal energy into electrical energy.
 
• **It is composed of several thermocouples connected usually in series or, less commonly, in parallel.**
 
• Thermopiles are used to measure the **temperature difference between two points, often the temperature of a surface and the temperature of the device itself.**
 
• **This difference can then be used to calculate the amount of heat energy received.**
 
• Applications of thermopiles** include gas leak detection, body temperature scanners, and industrial temperature measurement for kilns or gas turbine exhaust.**
 
 
 
• **Pyrometer Measures the temperature of a surface:**
 
 
• A **pyrometer **is a type of remote-sensing thermometer used to measure the temperature of a surface.
 
• The** term pyrometer was originally coined to denote a device capable of measuring temperatures of objects above incandescence (i.e., objects bright to the human eye).**
 
• **Pyrometers **are used in situations where** thermocouples are inadequate, such as in measuring the temperature of moving objects, objects in a vacuum, or very hot objects with temperatures above the range of thermocouples.**
 
• They are **commonly used in industrial applications such as steelmaking and ceramics production.**
